name: Question 18
problem: Which of the following represents the streamlines of the vector field $F(x,y)=(\frac{1}{y-{x}^{2}})i+(\frac{2x}{y-{x}^{2}})j$ over the domain $D=\{(x,y)\in {R}^{2}\,:\,y>{x}^{2}\}.$
worked_solution:
The streamlines of a vector field are the level curves of its stream function and are tangential to the vector field at every point. 

If $F$ represents the velocity field of a fluid flow, then they show the path traced out by a massless particle as it moves with the flow.

A vector field $F=P\,i+Q\,j$ with a simply connected domain $D⊆{R}^{2}$ has a stream function $ψ(x,y)$ if and only if

$$
\frac{∂P}{∂x}+\frac{∂Q}{∂y}=0.
$$

Note that 

$$
F(x,y)=(\frac{1}{y-{x}^{2}})i+(\frac{2x}{y-{x}^{2}})j
$$

 is a vector field with simply connected domain $D,$ where $P(x,y)=\frac{1}{y-{x}^{2}}$ and $Q(x,y)=\frac{2x}{y-{x}^{2}}.$ Computing the partial derivatives, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂P}{∂x}=\frac{2x}{(y-{x}^{2})^{2}},\,\frac{∂Q}{∂y} & =-\frac{2x}{(y-{x}^{2})^{2}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, $F$ has a stream function, since

$$
\frac{∂P}{∂x}+\frac{∂Q}{∂y}=\frac{2x}{(y-{x}^{2})^{2}}+(-\frac{2x}{(y-{x}^{2})^{2}})=0.
$$

Next, we find a stream function. A function $ψ(x,y)$ is a stream function of the vector field $F=P\,i+Q\,j$ if 

$$
P=\frac{∂ψ}{∂y},\,Q=-\frac{∂ψ}{∂x}.
$$

In our case, we have

$$
\frac{∂ψ}{∂y}=\frac{1}{y-{x}^{2}},\,\frac{∂ψ}{∂x}=-\frac{2x}{y-{x}^{2}}.
$$

Integrating these equations, we obtain the following:

$$
ψ(x,y)=\operatorname{ln}⁡(y-{x}^{2})+f(x),\,ψ(x,y)=\operatorname{ln}⁡(y-{x}^{2})+g(y)
$$

where $f$ and $g$ are arbitrary functions. Finally, setting $f=g=0,$ we have

$$
ψ(x,y)=\operatorname{ln}⁡(y-{x}^{2}).
$$

Finally, we find the level curves of the stream function $ψ(x,y)=\operatorname{ln}⁡(y-{x}^{2})$ given by the equations $ψ(x,y)=c.$

Notice that the range of $ψ(x,y)$ is $(-\infty ,\infty ).$ So, we will consider level curves for any value of $c.$ So, we have:

$$
\begin{aligned}ψ(x,y) & =c \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡(y-{x}^{2}) & =c \\ y-{x}^{2} & ={e}^{c} \\ y & ={x}^{2}+{e}^{c}\end{aligned}
$$

The equation above gives us a family of parabolas with the vertex at $(0,{e}^{c}).$ Therefore, the correct graph (along with the vector field $F$) is as follows:

If F represents the velocity field of a fluid flow, then they show the path traced out by a massless particle as it moves with the flow.

A vector field F=Pi+Qj with a simply connected domain D⊆R2 has a stream function ψ(x,y) if and only if ∂P∂x+∂Q∂y=0.

Note that F(x,y)=(1y−x2)i+(2xy−x2)j is a vector field with simply connected domain D, where P(x,y)=1y−x2 and Q(x,y)=2xy−x2. Computing the partial derivatives, we have

∂P∂x=2x(y−x2)2,∂Q∂y=−2x(y−x2)2.

Hence, F has a stream function, since

∂P∂x+∂Q∂y=2x(y−x2)2+(−2x(y−x2)2)=0.

Next, we find a stream function. A function ψ(x,y) is a stream function of the vector field F=Pi+Qj if

P=∂ψ∂y,Q=−∂ψ∂x.

In our case, we have ∂ψ∂y=1y−x2,∂ψ∂x=−2xy−x2.

ψ(x,y)=ln⁡(y−x2)+f(x),ψ(x,y)=ln⁡(y−x2)+g(y)

where f and g are arbitrary functions. Finally, setting f=g=0, we have

ψ(x,y)=ln⁡(y−x2).
